youtube.title: The Ocean's Top Killer Has Never Hunted You. Here's Why. #shorts
youtube.description:
The orca flips great white sharks, has killed adult blue whales and has rammed hundreds of boats, yet no wild orca has ever been documented killing a person. Its name is a myth: whalers called it the whale killer, but it is the biggest dolphin. A big male outweighs four cars, a pair off South Africa hunt great whites for their livers, and a pod off Western Australia took down the largest animal ever to live. Its brain is about four times heavier than yours, each family has its own dialect, and in 2018 one mother carried her dead calf for 17 days. The best guess for why it spares you: its sonar reads thin fat and the wrong bones, so you are not a seal and not food. The only orcas that have killed people lived in tanks.

In this video:
0:00 It has never hunted you. Why?
0:14 Four cars heavy, and the shark hunters
0:26 A blue whale, and a bigger brain
0:40 It grieves. Maybe it's friendly?
0:51 Hundreds of boats rammed
1:02 The likely answer: sonar
1:12 Only in tanks
1:22 Will you spare it?

Facts and sources:
- Orcas have flipped and held great white sharks upside down (Farallon Islands, 1997). Pyle, Schramm, Keiper & Anderson 1999, Marine Mammal Science 15(2): 563-568.
- Orcas kill white sharks off South Africa and eat the liver; sharks left Gansbaai for weeks to months afterwards. Towner et al. 2022, African Journal of Marine Science 44(2); Engelbrecht et al. 2019. "A pair of orcas" = the males known as Port and Starboard.
- First documented orca predation on adult blue whales, March 2019 off Bremer Bay, Western Australia. Totterdell et al. 2022, Marine Mammal Science 38(3).
- Name from Spanish whalers' "asesina-ballenas" (whale killer); the orca is the largest member of the dolphin family (Delphinidae). NOAA Fisheries "Killer Whale"; Encyclopaedia Britannica "killer whale".
- A big adult male weighs around 6 t (records to ~10 t); a mid-size car is ~1.5 t. NOAA Fisheries.
- Teeth up to ~7.5-10 cm long including root; an adult finger is ~7-8 cm. NOAA; SeaWorld/Busch Gardens Animal Info "Killer whale".
- Orca brain ~5.4-6.6 kg vs human ~1.3-1.4 kg (about four times heavier, not "smarter"). Ridgway & Hanson 2014, Brain, Behavior and Evolution 83.
- Resident orca pods have distinct, learned call dialects. Ford 1991, Canadian Journal of Zoology 69: 1454-1483.
- J35 (Tahlequah) carried her dead calf for 17 days, July-August 2018. Center for Whale Research; NOAA Fisheries 2018 updates.
- Iberian orca interactions since 2020: hundreds of boats contacted (over 500 by 2023), several sunk (at least 6 by 2024), no people injured. GT Orca Atlántica; Esteban et al. 2022, Marine Mammal Science; IWC 2023 workshop.
- The sonar explanation is a hypothesis, not proven (labelled BEST GUESS on screen). Odontocete echolocation can sense internal structure such as air spaces, bone and fat. Au 1993, The Sonar of Dolphins.
- 1972, Point Sur, California: a surfer was bitten by what is reported as an orca and released; the only widely cited wild bite. Wikipedia "Killer whale attacks on humans", citing period reports.
- No documented human death from a wild orca; all recorded deaths involved captive orcas. Wikipedia "Killer whale attacks on humans"; Kirby 2012, Death at SeaWorld.
- Tilikum was involved in three deaths: 1991 (Sealand of the Pacific), 1999 and 2010 (SeaWorld Orlando). OSHA v. SeaWorld 2012 decision; news archives.
- Ship noise masks orca echolocation and calls; Chinook salmon decline limits the Southern Residents. Holt et al. 2009, JASA; Veirs et al. 2016, PeerJ; NOAA Southern Resident Recovery Plan.
